climate.overview_html: Copernicus reports seven consecutive days above 2°C of warming from 18 to 24 November, a first. NOAA gives the El Niño about a 60% chance of becoming the strongest on record. COP31 ended without a cover decision, with talks resuming in Bonn in June.

items.headline: Global temperature stays above 2°C for seven straight days, Copernicus says
items.summary: Copernicus data show 18-24 November each ran more than 2°C above the 1850-1900 average for the date, the first such run on record. Reports put the 23 November anomaly near 2.25°C; Copernicus says this is not a breach of the Paris long-term threshold.

items.headline: NOAA gives the 2026-27 El Niño about a 60% chance of becoming the strongest on record
items.summary: NOAA's latest update says the event is still strengthening, with sea surface temperatures off Ecuador and Peru nearly 5°C above normal.

items.headline: COP31 ends without a cover decision for the first time since 2009
items.summary: At least 32 countries rejected the final draft of the proposed Antalya Pact. Narrower texts on Article 2.1(c) and the Climate Finance Work Programme were adopted, along with a step to channel carbon-market revenue into the UN Adaptation Fund. None set a figure for tripling adaptation finance.

items.headline: Development banks announce finance side deals as COP31 deadlocks
items.summary: Development banks and governments announced new climate finance initiatives outside the formal negotiations. Decisions on the just transition mechanism were deferred to 2027.

major_events.name: Southern Thailand monsoon rain
major_events.impact: TMD flags flash-flood risk in Surat Thani and Nakhon Si Thammarat and rough seas in the lower Gulf. Floods earlier in the week affected nearly 12,000 people, mostly in Phatthalung.

major_events.name: Thanksgiving storm aftermath, eastern US
major_events.impact: More than 500,000 customers were still without power on Friday. Virginia declared a state of emergency; one death is under investigation on Staten Island.

major_events.name: Western US mountain snow
major_events.status: Winter storm warnings through Sat night
major_events.impact: Colorado mountains expect 8-15 inches with gusts to 55 mph. An atmospheric river brings dense snow to the Cascades, northern Idaho and Montana, with another storm due Sunday.

major_events.name: Queensland severe storms
major_events.impact: BOM expects storms with heavy rain and damaging gusts moving from south-west to south-east Queensland, with the south-east most exposed on Sunday.

weather.overview_html: Southern Thailand faces another day of heavy rain, with the TMD warning 14 provinces of flash-flood risk. On the US East Coast, more than 500,000 customers were still without power on Friday after the Thanksgiving storm. Western mountains take the next system, with up to 15 inches of snow forecast for Colorado on Saturday. Queensland expects severe storms through Sunday. No tropical cyclones are active in the Atlantic or eastern Pacific.

items.headline: Thai Meteorological Department warns of heavy rain in 14 southern provinces
items.summary: The 5am bulletin puts the heaviest rain over Surat Thani and Nakhon Si Thammarat, with flash-flood risk in both. Residents near waterways and foothills are told to watch for overflows and landslides.

items.headline: Lower Gulf of Thailand seas turn rough as upper Thailand cools
items.summary: TMD paired the southern rain warning with rough-sea advice for the lower Gulf, while a cool air mass lowers temperatures over the north and northeast.

items.headline: More than 500,000 still without power a day after the Thanksgiving storm
items.summary: Outages and rain continued along the East Coast on Friday. Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger declared a state of emergency to support recovery.

items.headline: Body recovered from a submerged vehicle on Staten Island after the storm
items.summary: Police found a man's body after a vehicle was reported underwater near a coastal roadway on Thanksgiving. The cause of death was not immediately determined.

items.headline: Colorado mountains under winter storm warning for up to 15 inches of snow
items.summary: The NWS warning runs from Friday evening through Saturday night, with 8-15 inches and gusts to 55 mph. Forecasters advise travelling on Friday or Sunday instead of Saturday.

items.headline: Atmospheric river carries dense snow from the Cascades into the Northern Rockies
items.summary: The storm brings snow to the Washington and Oregon Cascades, southeast British Columbia, northern Idaho and Montana through Saturday. In Bend, another storm returns Sunday after a brief Saturday break.

items.headline: Thanksgiving storms leave nearly a million US customers without power
items.summary: Outages across the East Coast neared one million customers, and more than 400 US flights were cancelled on the holiday.

items.headline: Severe storms forecast for Queensland through the weekend
items.summary: The Bureau of Meteorology expects severe storms from Friday in south-west Queensland, spreading to the south-east by Sunday with heavy rain and damaging gusts. It also forecasts a hot, dry summer under El Niño.

renewables.overview_html: China's installed solar reached about 1.33 TW at the end of October. France tripled its next renewable auction to 1.5 GW. In South Australia, storm-downed transmission keeps the Cathedral Rocks wind farm offline while temporary towers go up.

items.headline: China's cumulative solar capacity reaches about 1.33 TW
items.summary: NEA data put installed solar at roughly 1.33 TW at the end of October, up 16.3% year on year. China Huaneng also started a 400 MW offshore solar project in Jiangsu sharing sea area with a working wind farm.

items.headline: France triples its planned renewable auction to 1.5 GW
items.summary: The technology-neutral tender rises from 500 MW to 1.5 GW and opens to all renewable technologies, the government said on 25 November.

items.headline: Sungrow and EVE Energy among six new storage orders and bid wins
items.summary: The roundup includes a 380 MW/1,500 MWh project in Spain involving Sungrow's renewables arm and a 1.2 GWh EVE Energy cooperation deal.

items.headline: Global residential storage shipments reach 57.58 GWh in the first nine months of 2026
items.summary: Home battery shipments worldwide totalled 57.58 GWh from January to September 2026.

items.headline: Egypt targets 31.9 GW of renewables and 14.42 GWh of storage by 2030
items.summary: Egypt set a 2030 goal of 31.9 GW of renewable capacity paired with 14.42 GWh of battery storage.

items.headline: Eyre Peninsula to reconnect by Friday on temporary transmission towers
items.summary: Crews are building temporary towers after a storm downed two and damaged a third; permanent replacements could take up to a year. The 62 MW Cathedral Rocks wind farm stays offline and a rooftop solar export ban remains, as winds exceeded the towers' design limits.

science.overview_html: Two reviews of AI weather prediction landed this week: a Nature Reviews survey of 2015-2025 work and an npj assessment of foundation models and LLM decision tools. A GRL study links cloud-top charge to droplet size in layer clouds, and an Earth's Future paper projects 76-140% more lightning by 2100 under high emissions.

items.headline: Review maps a decade of AI for short-to-medium range weather prediction
items.summary: The review covers machine-learning weather prediction from 2015 to 2025 and sets out recommendations for future research.

items.headline: Review assesses weather foundation models and LLM decision support
items.summary: The authors searched four databases for studies from January 2020 to May 2026 on foundation models in forecasting and LLM-based tools that turn forecasts into decisions.

items.headline: Aircraft profiles show cloud-top charge in layer clouds tracks droplet size
items.summary: Clouds with more charge at their tops tended to contain larger droplets. The link could matter for how droplets collide and grow toward drizzle.

items.headline: Lightning could become 76-140% more common by 2100 under high emissions
items.meta: Andreas Krause (TUM) et al. · Earth's Future
items.summary: The projection compares the end of the century with 1995-2014. More lightning raises ignition risk for wildfires.

items.headline: NOAA study suggests flying G-IV hurricane missions closer to storm centers
items.summary: The study quantifies the forecast impact of all reconnaissance data from NOAA's Gulfstream IV-SP jet, which has mostly sampled storm outskirts.

items.headline: Slower Atlantic overturning shrank the North Pacific's low-oxygen zone in the ice age
items.summary: Fossil shells from 11 sediment cores show the North Pacific oxygen minimum zone shrank, sometimes almost vanishing, during iceberg surges that slowed Atlantic overturning. The reconstruction carries a ±45% error margin and uses a coarse model.

items.headline: Ocean iodine will not offset future ozone pollution, study finds
items.summary: York and UEA researchers project that iodine's ozone-removing and cooling effects stall by 2100 and weaken slightly, even as Arctic Ocean iodine emissions rise 143%.
items.meta: University of York, UEA · Science Advances

items.headline: Study probes why India and southern China set heat records together in May 2026
items.summary: A team led by Gao Meng at Hong Kong Baptist University, with the Chinese Academy of Meteorological Sciences and NUIST, analyzed the intensity, duration and drivers of the concurrent heatwaves and assessed the human contribution.
items.meta: Hong Kong Baptist University · Advances in Atmospheric Sciences

items.headline: Pangu, FengWu and FuXi tested on Oklahoma tornado environments
items.summary: Across ten strong-tornado events, Pangu-Weather handled storm-relative helicity well, while FuXi Weather did well on several thermodynamic parameters but overpredicted their magnitude.

items.title: Weatherstack moves sign-ups and billing onto the APILayer platform
items.body_html: Weatherstack's real-time, historical, forecast and marine endpoints are now sold through APILayer accounts, alongside the company's other APIs. Existing keys, subscriptions and endpoints keep working; new customers sign up through APILayer. It is a distribution change, not a new data product.

items.title: BBC switches its forecast supply back to the Met Office, replacing MeteoGroup
items.body_html: The BBC's Met Office partnership went live on 26 November, ending a supply deal with MeteoGroup, now part of DTN, that began in 2018. The BBC app and site add hourly 10-day forecasts and push alerts for Met Office warnings, and a BBC weather centre opens at the Met Office in Exeter.

items.title: ECMWF director cites Chongqing's Pangu-based rain warnings as a model
items.body_html: ECMWF's director visited Chongqing, where a Huawei-assisted AI model built on Pangu supports heavy-rainfall warnings up to six hours ahead. Chongqing's bureau already runs a 1 km hourly AI forecast for the Chengdu-Chongqing region.

items.title: Mesotech wins Air Force weather station contract worth up to $26.5M
items.body_html: Rancho Cordova-based Mesotech International won a five-year contract worth up to $26.5 million to maintain Air Force weather stations. Mesotech already holds a $31.3 million fixed-base weather system award from 2023.

items.title: SenseNet raises $43M to expand its wildfire detection network
items.body_html: Idealist Capital led the Series B financing, which mixes new equity, secondary sales and debt. SenseNet combines ground sensors, AI cameras, satellite data and predictive analytics, and says its monitored area grew from 130 million to over 450 million acres in a year.

items.title: Northrop Grumman wins $290.6M NASA contract for NOAA NEON microwave sounders
items.body_html: NASA awarded Northrop Grumman $290.6 million to build three Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications instruments for NOAA's Near Earth Orbit Network, with work running to April 2042. The government program of record sits alongside NOAA's commercial microwave-sounder data buys from Spire, Tomorrow.io and others.
